about: The ledger contract: every event kind in ledger.jsonl, the script that writes it (or the list of scripts that do), and its fields.

Each field's type is string, number, array (a list), numbers (a list of whole numbers, 0 or more), object or id (a Discord id: a string of digits, which --check also takes as a whole number, the form team-log wrote before), or a list of the strings it may be.
Every line has ts (UTC, like 2026-10-22T01:00:00Z), task (T<n>) and event; note (a string) is allowed on every kind, and other fields are allowed.
A kind's field_writers names the one script that may append a line holding each field it lists, among the kind's writers; the others append the kind without it.

A kind with push true records Daniel's word or an outside fact, so the script that appends it commits the ledger and pushes it to the team home's origin at once (ledger_push), not at the next checkpoint.

A kind's field_when names, for each field it lists, the values another field must hold for a line to carry it, as {"discord_message": {"role": ["ops"]}}: a line holding the field with any other value there is refused.
A kind's one_of lists sets of fields of which a line carries exactly one, as [["text", "chars"]]: a line holding none of a set (an empty string counting as none), or more than one, is refused.
Lines from strict_from on must meet their kind's fields; earlier lines are legacy and only need ts, task and event.
Legacy lines keep shapes no kind has now: closes by hand with no lists, and plan-ready, which is not a kind, since a planner's report is done and a plan put to Daniel is asked.
Read by ledger_append in bin/lib/team.sh (through bin/lib/ledger.jq) and printed by team-log --help.

opened.about: story is the backlog story the task builds (team-open --story), which team-merge marks done

interview-thread.about: team-thread --interview: the task's thread under the interview channel, where a planner interviews Daniel

launch.about: request is the link to Daniel's Discord message, on an ops launch, and discord_message its id, a message no other ops launch ran on (team-worker refuses one that did), which only an ops launch carries; model is the --model the session launched on, from the project's models in the registry, absent on the default; brief is the file name without .md of the first brief*.md the prompt names directly under the task's tasks/T<n>/, absent when it names none there; admission is the id of the capacity admission the launch was made on (team-capacity admit's first line), absent on T0, ops and a launch from before 2026-11-11; past_ask is the ids of the open asks the launch went past (team-worker --past-ask), which then park nothing, absent when it names none

closed.about: a legacy task's lists are empty; the hand-written legacy closes before strict_from have none

merged.about: approval: the word it merged on, head (a merge-approved of the PR at its head) or default (the task's approved plan), and for history plan (a merge-preapproved of its project, retired) or standing (Daniel's merge-standing, retired); by, discord_message and discord_channel name Daniel's Discord message, or on a plan the coordinator approved, by says so with the approval's time and the two are left out; phases_left: the phases of the task with a ticket not done when the PR merged, from team-tickets, [] when every ticket was done, absent for a task with no tickets or whose tickets could not be read; a non-empty list makes the task a merged part (bin/lib/lifecycle.json), whose next phase is still to build

gate-lane-cleared.about: the branch's ref was deleted from the gate's mirror after a rewrite; head, the mirror's head it held; tag, the mirror's ref that keeps it

caught-up.about: url is the PR's; from, the reviewed head whose review the merge stands on, the merge made onto it or onto an earlier catch-up of it; head, that merge, pushed as the PR's head; base, the base's commit it merged; all full shas

done.about: a worker's report; an ops session's carries report_chars, its report's length in characters, never its text, and relay, the coordinator's message in Discord that relayed it

question.about: a worker's question; an ops session's carries chars, its length in characters, never its text, and discord_message, the question's first message in the task's thread when team-ask put it to Daniel

asked.about: a decision put to Daniel; discord_message: the question's first message in the task's thread, which team-inbox links; script and sha256: a script Daniel is asked to OK and its sha256sum, which the question names, logged together by team-ask --script, their one writer, which team-run-approved runs only once Daniel's latest answer to the ask, read back from Discord, has a line that starts with yes, or, when that answered names an item, a part with that number, every such part starting with yes, and only while the file hashes the same

answered.about: Daniel's answer to the asked of its id; discord_message: the message team-answer read it from, never logged twice for one ask; item: the waiting list's number Daniel's message answered it by, logged by team-answer --item alone

ran.about: an approved script run once its ask was answered: id the asked naming it, exit its exit code; its output is in the machine's ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agent-team/runs/T<n>/<id>.log, never in the records

plan-approved.about: the task's plan approved by Daniel, with ask the asked it answers and discord_message their message, which team-log requires of every new line of theirs, or by the coordinator, with neither; plan each file approved, the team home's tasks/T<n>/plan.md and the task directory's spec.md and scope.txt (plan_files in bin/lib/team.sh), to its sha256, and scope scope.txt's lines, both written by team-log itself; a line with no plan is from before T276, read as the coordinator's whatever its by (plan_approval in bin/lib/ledger.jq); it stands until a later plan-approval-withdrawn

plan-approval-withdrawn.about: Daniel withdrew the task's standing plan approval in discord_message, which stops its build until the plan is approved again; team-log takes whatever message it names, since it only stops work

paused.about: a worker's or the task's work paused; cause: why, a cause bin/lib/lifecycle.json gives paused, which team-log requires of every new line it logs; role and session: the paused worker's, when the line names one; brief: on team-worker's own room refusal (cause room, its role the launch's), the brief the refused launch named; since: when the park began, when it is logged after the fact

blocked.about: a worker stopped by an obstacle; it stands until a launch or a resumed id= or all=true ends it, by its cause's rules in bin/lib/lifecycle.json (a worker's block that names its role only at a launch of that role), an old line with no cause as before; cause: why, a cause bin/lib/lifecycle.json gives blocked, task when on names a task, else worker unless given; role and session: the blocked worker's, when the line names one; since: when the park began, when it is logged after the fact

denied.about: a denial the worker went past (a permission rule, a hook, auto mode): what was denied and why; it parks nothing and clears nothing, and team-time and team-retro count it as a denial; a denial that stops the work is a blocked; denial-log, every worker's PermissionDenied hook, logs each denial auto mode makes, what the tool's name and why the rule's bracketed label or no verdict, never the tool's input

held.about: Daniel's hold on the task; cause: daniel-hold; discord_message: Daniel's message saying so, which team-log requires of every new line; since: when the park began, when it is logged after the fact

waiting.about: a task parked on Daniel or something outside the team; it stands until a launch or a resumed id= or all=true ends it, but team-ask's wait on its ask, which only that ask's answered ends, an old line with no cause as before; cause: why, a cause bin/lib/lifecycle.json gives waiting, daniel when on is Daniel (any case), else outside unless given, and ask for team-ask's wait on its ask, whose id ask names; since: when the park began, when it is logged after the fact

resumed.about: ends standing parks, by bin/lib/lifecycle.json's causes: id, the park it ends (team-state's parks name each), Daniel's hold only with discord_message, Daniel's message lifting it, and an ask's wait never; all true, every park whose cause takes all; brief alone, the file name without .md of the brief the holder was sent, on a merge-base round, which holds team-sweep's merge-due, ends none; an old line with none of the three ended every park

review.about: verdict: findings whenever sent_back names a finding, whatever the reviewer's word, since a pass whose notes go back is not ready to merge (team-log logs it so); sent_back: the numbers of the findings sent back to the builder before the merge, each a blocking finding, a correctness, security or real-data note, or a plain note on a line the PR adds or changes, never one before lists; findings: the count of each kind, exactly blocking, correctness, security, real-data, note-change (plain notes on lines the PR adds or changes) and note-before (plain notes on code it did not change), each a whole number; before: the numbers of the plain notes on code the PR did not change, each queued as a follow-up; guarded: the guarded areas the reviewer found the change touching, each one of ci, dependencies, migrations, settings, permissions, secrets and guardrails (the team's own guards: bin/lib/guarded, team-merge, team-checks, the library code they run, team-heavy, the ledger contract, data-check, records, the hooks and the sessions' settings files), empty for none; widening: the numbers of the new findings that sit in what the last fix added for an earlier finding, so reverting that fix would end them, as a rereview marks them; empty for none; memory: the file in the task directory of the memories the reviewer added there for the coordinator to file in the project's memory at close, since the hook refuses a reviewer the memory directory

gate-run.about: one per gate run, at its end: run is the gate's run id, head the commit it ran on, cause why it repeats an earlier run on the same PR, minutes each step's minutes as no-mistakes axi status --run prints them, approved the ids of the parks the builder approved itself in the run, each a kind its brief or the project's review rules name (team-time counts them), absent when it approved none

merge-approved.about: Daniel's word on the PR at url, one of the task's pr events, at head, the full sha the ask named, which a pr event of url, or a review of the task since url's first pr event, logged, its discord_message sent no earlier than the first of those that logged it; team-log requires head of every new line, and earlier lines without it hold for any head; legacy lines name only the number

merge-preapproved.about: Daniel's plan-time word on the task's PR in project, its discord_message an answer to the task's latest asked of id ask, sent no earlier than it, which it settles; scope the repository paths the plan may change, each a file or a directory ending in /; it stands until a later merge-preapproval-withdrawn of project, and the latest of a project is the one read

merge-preapproval-withdrawn.about: Daniel withdrew the task's latest merge-preapproved of project, in discord_message

merge-standing.about: Daniel's standing word that the team may merge a ready PR of project, never the team's own (own_project), which team-log refuses, or of every other project when project is all, with no ask, said in discord_message in discord_channel, #coordinator's channel or the task's thread; read across the whole ledger, the task only naming the thread: for a project, the latest merge-standing or merge-standing-withdrawn whose project is that project or all decides, and the word stands when that is a merge-standing

merge-standing-withdrawn.about: Daniel withdrew the standing word on project, or on every project but the team's own when project is all, in discord_message in discord_channel; read with merge-standing across the whole ledger, so a withdrawal of one project leaves a word on all standing for the others, and a later merge-standing stands again

branch-renamed.about: the task's branch in project is branch from now on, as when the gate rewrote the remote branch and the builder carried its commits to a new one; the latest opened, worktree-added or branch-renamed of the project names the task's branch there

retro-schedule.about: Daniel's word on how often a retro runs, read by team-retro from the latest across the ledger; every_hours 0 stops the retros

retro-change.about: the task it is logged on builds those proposals of retro T<m>, or, logged on T<m> itself, records were changed in place for them; proposals as Daniel's answer names them; team-retro digest reads when each landed, for the next retro to judge

stowing.about: a stow of the task under way on machine, logged by team-stow --begin before the coordinator sends its workers STOW (the level and handoff skills), or by a team-stow run that finds none standing, after its branches check and before it stops any session: cause level or handoff, as the run's; roles the task's unfinished work then (ledger.jq's unfinished_roles), which a stow-failed keeps for the resume; it stands until the task's stowed or stow-failed, or a launch, and team-sweep names one standing 30 minutes

stowed.about: one per task team-stow stows, every open task at a handoff (team-handoff runs team-stow --all --cause handoff), which wrote it itself before 2026-11-02: worktrees as {project, branch, head}, with uncommitted: true for one whose changes the checkpoint kept as wip/<project>/T<n> on the team home's origin; roles the task's unfinished work, each role launched since its last stowed that nothing ended (ledger.jq's unfinished_roles), which the other machine or the resume relaunches; sessions the roles whose sessions the stow stopped, for the record (before 2026-10-25, roles held those); cause level for a stow to free the machine for the team's resource level, handoff (or absent, as in every line before team-stow) for a handoff

stow-failed.about: a stow of the task under way (its stowing) that team-stow did not finish on machine: reason the refusal of the task by a step after the stowing (a diverged branch, a session that would not stop, a push), or "the run stopped: <its last error line>" when a step stopped the run (a checkpoint that failed, exit 1 or 75); the task is then read as stowed with the stowing's roles, so the resume relaunches them, until a launch

worktree-moved.about: team-open --resume, when this machine's worktree for the task in project is not the recorded one

injection.about: outside text that asked role to act: source is where it was (a URL, a path, a command, or <collection>/<_id>), text what it asked, never the personal details it held

rehome-failed.about: a worktree of the task in project that team-open --resume could not make on machine, reason the first line team-open printed; it stands until a later opened, worktree-added, worktree-moved, rehomed or worktree-returned of the task in project

rehomed.about: team-open --resume, when it makes the worktree at its recorded path while a rehome-failed of the task in project stands; made anywhere else, the worktree-moved clears it

walk.about: a manual QC walk of the task turned on or off (team-ui --walk start or stop), only when that changes it: the walk is on while the task's latest walk is on and the task is not closed, since its ts, and while it is on each message of Daniel's in the task's thread is a walk note the coordinator captures the page with

image-posted.about: one image team-post --attach sent: its thread, the message holding it and its base name; a message of several images has one line each, and what left the machine is never removed from the ledger

image-retracted.about: team-post --retract deleted the message discord_message, which image-posted lines of the task record; a copy Discord's CDN holds may outlive it
